correctness.rationale: The normalized beta moments and angular Fourier orthogonality give an exact diagonal Gram operator. The continuous profile follows from gamma-ratio asymptotics including the n/k=0,1 boundaries. Uniform near-zero and n>=2k derivative bounds control the norm, Schatten tail and superlevel counting limits. The derivative of F_p reduces the unique peak classification to g_p(y) with g_p′(y)=2(1-py)/(1-y^2), and exact p=1 and p=3 calculations check the boundary and special values. An executable finite checker independently tests rational moments, the exact alpha=0 finite formula and asymptotic samples. Numerical experiments are not offered as proof.

value.rationale: Varying the degree of the anti-holomorphic symbol while resolving analytic modes on the same scale measures how Bergman projection leakage is redistributed, a natural finite-frequency filtering question. The exact continuum spectral law determines all positive thresholds and all Schatten q>1 leading coefficients, whereas the known trace identity gives only total leakage. The transition from n/k=1 for alpha<=0 to a unique interior maximizer for alpha>0, with a golden-ratio case at alpha=2, is a structural and non-obvious change in the geometry of the most unstable analytic mode.
